notes: Rules graded: the eight rows of the evals/README.md index whose Cases cell names macro-dsl, the seven macro and library rules of the previous sweep plus the do: rule, which was added after db91c23 and so has no verdict in <previous>/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json.

git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only SKILL.md (the one-step with rule, the new do: rule, the captures rule) and references/testing.md (Assert with patterns). macros.md and library-design.md are unchanged, so the seven macro and library rules are graded to the standard of the previous sweep's macro-dsl grade files: a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, validation in the macro body outside quote does not; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them; `if not ... raise` validation is not counted under the branching rule; a one-line three-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; generated routes/0 and match/1 without @doc are not counted.

Changed rule (new since db91c23), graded against its current text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability): Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. Its text is unchanged since the check-3 batch (git diff 8d4ba29 HEAD -- idiomatic-elixir/ is empty), so it is graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-check-3/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json. Violating runs out of five, per sentence. "Use `do:` for a body of one expression that reads as part of the head": 0 of 5. "A body with several steps, a `case` or `with`, or a comment gets `do ... end`.": 0 of 5. "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line.": 0 of 5 (every mixed function sets its block clauses apart). "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.": 1 of 5 (sonnet-1, validate_path!/2: one do: clause and two block clauses whose one-expression bodies would wrap under do:, 135 and 143 characters). "A one-expression body too long for the head's line wants a block or a helper; a head that `mix format` wraps because of a long guard is fine as wrapped.": 1 of 5 (haiku-2, match_segments/3 lines 93-94 and 96-97, where mix format moved a too-long body onto a do: line under a head with no guard). Any sentence: 2 of 5 (haiku-2, sonnet-1). Line lengths checked with Code.format_string! on the do: form of each block clause.

match_segments/3 is written as four clauses in all five runs; opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 keep the two short clauses on do: and write the two recursive clauses as blocks set apart by blank lines (two of four is not most, so clean, as at check-3); haiku-2 writes the two recursive clauses as wrapped do: lines instead. sonnet-2 writes all four clauses of __define__/3 as blocks; each would wrap under do: (126 to 182 characters), and its first clause's head is wrapped by a long guard, which the rule accepts.
Runs: result.json gives head 0397dec with uncommitted false for all five; the skill copy the runs read (scratchpad/sweep3/root/skill) is identical to the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace in scratch Mix projects (one per run, the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, so xref line numbers match the run file, with real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex, except for sonnet-2, whose file defines its own stubs). opus-1 (Macro.expand_literals with function {:match, 1}), sonnet-1 ({:__routes__, 0}) and sonnet-2 ({:routes, 0}) report alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime). haiku-1 and haiku-2 do not expand the handler and pass the alias into a function that get's quote calls in the router's module body, and xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile), the route of the previous sweep's skill-haiku-2.

Bad-declaration checks: each run's file loaded, then one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and another declaring get "/", "not a module" compiled with Code.compile_string. All ten fail while the router compiles: opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 with ArgumentError from the function get's quote calls; sonnet-1 with CompileError raised while get expands. Messages below omit the nofile:3: location prefix.
Format: all five pass mix format --check-formatted (all five wrote get("/", MyApp.PageHandler) with parentheses) and compile without warnings with elixir and with mix compile.

Reads: all five read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md before writing the file. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 used one Read call per file; opus-1 and sonnet-1 read both references with one cat in a Bash call. This matches result.json reads and satisfies the Expected reads line.

Against the previous sweep's skill runs: per_rule is unchanged on the seven macro and library rules (Keep quote blocks small violated by Sonnet only, the compile-time-dependency rule by Haiku only). Both haiku runs now pass the alias unexpanded (the previous haiku-1 used Macro.expand); sonnet-1 again writes the attribute directly in get's quote; opus-1 and sonnet-2 are clean on all eight rules. Four of five runs again write the one-line three-step pipeline in __before_compile__; sonnet-2 splits it over lines.

Smoke test outside the rules: all five return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope"; haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 return atom param keys (%{id: "42"}), opus-1 and sonnet-2 string keys (%{"id" => "42"}).
